key_insight: Injecting per-frame learnable camera tokens and a lightweight pose regression signal into a video multimodal LLM grounds frames in a shared 3D coordinate frame, enabling more consistent, geometry-aware video understanding.
problem_solved: Multimodal LLMs treat video frames as isolated 2D snapshots and lack persistent camera-pose information, causing poor spatio-temporal consistency and limited 3D scene reasoning across frames.
method: Introduce per-frame learnable camera tokens that represent viewpoint (position & orientation) and are attached to each frame's representation.
Add a lightweight pose-regression head and supervisory signal to learn pose embeddings, and fuse pose tokens into the video encoder + multimodal fusion pipeline.
Use pose-conditioned temporal modeling so the LLM reasons about observations in a shared spatial coordinate frame for improved cross-frame consistency and scene understanding.
impact: Provides a simple, compatible way to make video MLLMs geometry-aware, improving temporal consistency and 3D reasoning for applications like robotics, AR, and embodied AI without major architectural overhaul.
visual_elements: Timeline of video frames with overlaid camera pose vectors/tokens showing a shared 3D coordinate frame
Architecture diagram: video encoder → per-frame camera tokens + pose regression head → multimodal fusion with LLM
Before/after example panels: baseline (pose-agnostic) vs Cambrian-P outputs illustrating corrected spatial reasoning
Bar chart or table summarizing metric improvements (consistency, localization, reasoning) from pose grounding
